page: Microsoft Azure M128-64bds_3_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32 physical cores (64 vCPUs with 2 threads per core), a 105 MB L3 cache, and a massive 2794.0 GB of system memory, yielding 43.66 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 6144 GB of local disk capacity and is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations highlight top-tier memory bandwidth performance, with large-block read-only speeds reaching 367.66 GB/sec and write speeds at 169.25 GB/sec. Single-core performance is strong, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2203.0 and top-tier results in image and text processing. Multi-core performance is also robust, with a Passmark CPU score of 81742.61 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 67529.51. Database operations are highly efficient, scoring 35100.58 in Passmark database tests and achieving 87.35 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. However, single-core stress-ng performance (2059.48) and Passmark memory score (2422.33) fall into the average tier.

Given its high resource density, particularly the massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and substantial local storage, this server offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads requiring large in-memory footprints without needing proportional scaling of compute cores. The presence of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) supports accelerated mathematical operations, making it suitable for CPU-based LLM inference, where it achieves 32.46 tokens/sec for large 70B model prompt processing. This server is highly suited for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data analytics, and memory-intensive enterprise applications.
